On Tuesday, I had the honor of joining Connecticut leaders at the State Capitol for a ceremony to honor and remember Lt. Governor Nancy Wyman, one of our state’s finest public servants.

As a PTA mom in Tolland, a State Representative, State Comptroller, and Lieutenant Governor, Nancy was an amazing model for all of us in patience, basic decency, respect, and empathy. That is especially true in today’s political climate.

Nancy and I came into the Connecticut General Assembly in the same election with neighboring districts in Tolland County, and we sat next to each other in the General Assembly Chamber. Together, we accomplished a lot for the people we represented, such as passage of prescription drug assistance for Connecticut seniors years before Medicare Part D was enacted. It was an honor to have a front-row seat to her public service.

I’m proud to have called Nancy a friend, as well as the Wyman family, and like so many she came into contact with, I will cherish her memory.

On Thursday, I joined Habitat for Humanity of Eastern CT at their “Building Hope & Homes” celebration for 14 new homes built by the non-profit in Norwich supporting 16 families.
 
I was honored to receive the Habitat Hero Award for my work to secure $900,000 in federal funding that supported construction of the homes. It was great to met with Leslie Souvenance, the owner of the 14th home built using the funding, alongside Habitat’s Executive Director Sarah Lufler and Norwich Mayor Swarnjit Singh.

Back in 2021, I strongly supported passage of the American Rescue Plan Act, a bill that provided $900,000 in funding to Habitat for Humanity of Eastern CT, which Habitat used to support the construction of the 16 homes. 

The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which I helped pass this summer, will allow Habitat for Humanity of Eastern CT to expand their model for new home construction. Congress needs to deliver on the ROAD to Housing Act’s reforms with robust investment in housing programs.

roll_calls.plain_language: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act establishes and modifies various federal housing programs. This vote, under suspension of the rules, was on accepting the Senate's latest changes to the bill after the chambers traded versions, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea accepts the Senate's version; a Nay opposes it.

post.text:
Eastern Connecticut needs more quality affordable homes to meet demand and lower costs.

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
